newsitem.title: USA: Sands in loan default, cites revenue slump.
newsitem.headline: Sands in loan default, cites revenue slump.

text.p: Sands Regent Inc said because of a decline in revenues and profitability it was not in compliance with a financial covenant, resulting in a default under a loan agreement.
The covenant was part of a long-term debt loan agreement, the company said. The balance of this debt obligation was about $11 million, it said.
The company reported second quarter revenues of $13.5 million versus $14.0 million.
Sands, which owns and operates hotel casino complexes, said it was in talks with the lender about the situation.

"Like most of our Reno area competitors, our revenues at the Sands Regency in Reno continue to be depressed because of the increased competition from Las Vegas and the increase in Reno hotel/casino facilities," Pete Cladianos, Jr., company president, said.
The company was completing a renovation of its Reno casino and other public area facilities to enhance its competitive position, he said.
"However, the timing of any improvements in revenue and profitability at our Reno hotel/casino is difficult to project given the overall depressed market conditions," Cladianos said.
Sands was also incurring additional costs in order to improve its Mississippi facilities, he said.
"The Copa Casino will also incur costs and expenses for some deferred maintenane of its facilities, including the requirement for sinificant dredging under and around the Copa vessel," he said.
Its operations there were also jeopardized by ongoing litigation, he said.

In August, Sands said it filed a suit against the Mississippi Port Authority and Mississippi Department of Economic Development because they refused to give Copa clearance to expand its casino operations in Gulfport, Mississippi.
